parameters.label: Configuration source
parameters.description: inherit reads the original entry when present; own reads this entry. Switching does not copy values.

parameters.label: Map ID
parameters.description: Existing map used whenever the normal title scene is entered. The plugin starts fresh temporary new-game state and transfers the player to MapID at MapX/MapY; map events provide the title interface instead of the native title command window.
parameters.context: Enable Coreto_4_EventTitleScene 0.1.0 with event-title-scene install after its optional providers/consumers have been arranged; the bundle must already be delivered. install selects this provider instead of VisuMZ_4_EventTitleScene and preserves other provider selections. Restart the game after configuration changes. Core Engine and Message Core are optional: if used, enable one supported provider of each before this plugin (Coreto_0_CoreEngine 0.1.0 / VisuMZ_0_CoreEngine 1.90; Coreto_1_MessageCore 0.1.0 / VisuMZ_1_MessageCore 1.57). Place it after active Options Core, Save Core, Picture Choices, VN Picture Busts, Choice Common Events and Attached Pictures, and before Message Visibility. The CLI edits js/plugins.js for the next game boot; it does not change an already running game. parameters reset and missing native values use this entry's published default. parameters get reports the effective value; event-title-scene api describe CORETO-CONFIG-SOURCE explains inherit/own. Choose a whole map database ID in 1..999 from data/MapInfos.json with a corresponding data/MapNNN.json file, for example Map001.json for ID 1. The schema accepts fractional numbers but those do not identify a normal map file. The selected map must contain your title UI events (for example an Autorun Show Choices event calling ET-C-NewGame, ET-C-LoadScreen and ET-C-Options). Check MapX/MapY against its dimensions. Returning from Options or cancelling Load into the title reconstructs this map with fresh game state; changes made during the previous title visit are discarded. Title-map autosave, random encounters, normal menu input and debug input are disabled. This does not replace the database starting map used by NewGame. The CLI edits configuration and does not create the map or its events.

parameters.label: Map X
parameters.description: Player starting X tile coordinate (column, increasing to the right) on the map selected by MapID when the evented title scene starts.
parameters.context: Use a whole tile coordinate with zero at the top-left tile of the selected map. Choose a tile inside that map as well as within the published numeric limits. This sets the player transfer destination, not a pixel offset of the title artwork. The paired MapX/MapY parameters determine the destination even when PlayerTransparent hides the player. The CLI edits js/plugins.js for the next game boot; it does not change an already running game. parameters reset and missing native values use this entry's published default. parameters get reports the effective value; event-title-scene api describe CORETO-CONFIG-SOURCE explains inherit/own. See event-title-scene api describe ET-P-MapID:num for activation, map selection and title-state reset on reentry. This parameter is applied when the title map is prepared; runtime event commands may subsequently change player state.

parameters.label: Face Direction
parameters.description: Initial player facing passed to the title-map transfer: 2 down, 4 left, 6 right, 8 up; 1 down-left, 3 down-right, 7 up-left and 9 up-right request diagonals. Use 2/4/6/8 for ordinary native four-direction character sheets. Diagonal rendering needs a compatible movement/sprite provider; Coreto Events Move supports a [VS8] sheet (events-move api describe EV-P-VS8), and converts diagonals to cardinal facing for ordinary sheets. This affects facing, not the transfer coordinates.

parameters.label: Transparent?
parameters.description: When true, hide the player character on the title map; when false, show the configured party leader sprite. This does not remove the player, disable event interaction or control movement (see ET-P-CanInputMove:eval). Native followers copy player transparency, so true also prevents visible followers even when ShowFollowers is enabled.

parameters.label: Can Input Move?
parameters.description: When true, allow the normal player directional and map-touch movement checks on the title map; events or other native restrictions can still block movement. When false, suppress player direction input and map-touch destinations there. Scripted movement/routes are not disabled. This setting does not enable menu input or encounters.

parameters.label: Show Followers?
parameters.description: When true, enable the follower group on the title map; visible followers still require additional party battle members and PlayerTransparent=false. When false, hide the follower group. It does not add party actors or override each follower copying the player transparency.

commands.label: System: Start New Game
commands.description: Discard current game state and start a new game at the database starting position, not the title MapID. With Save Core locked style, first reset state and open the save-slot picker; selecting a slot starts that new game, while cancelling returns to a fresh title map when called there. Without locked style, use the transition scene to reset and enter Scene_Map. No save file is written by this command itself.

args.label: Slow Fade Out?
args.description: JavaScript expression encoded as a JSON string, such as "true", "false" or "$gameSwitches.value(1)". A truthy result calls the current scene fadeOutAll before changing scene; false skips this extra fade and leaves any destination-scene transition behavior intact. Native fadeOutAll fades screen, BGM, BGS and ME over slowFadeSpeed (normally 48 update frames, about 0.8 seconds at 60 updates/s).

javascript.context: Evaluated once when the event command executes, before scene selection. No callback arguments or local bindings are supplied. The CLI compiles syntax only; runtime errors propagate. A truthy result invokes currentScene.fadeOutAll; the expression does not choose the destination scene.

args.context: Argument of event-title-scene api describe ET-C-NewGame. This is authored as a string even though the editor presents a boolean. The CLI validates syntax without evaluating it; use a boolean result. The transition itself still occurs for false.

commands.label: System: Open Load Scene
commands.description: With standard/locked save style (or no Save Core), push Scene_Load for slot selection; cancelling returns to the previous scene class, rebuilding fresh title-map state when invoked from the title. With Save Core single style, attempt slot 0 directly instead of showing a slot list. Missing saves report load failure; a failed asynchronous load returns to a fresh evented title map. A successful load restores the saved game and enters Scene_Map.

tags.label: Continue choice
tags.description: In any native Show Choices label, <Continue> keeps that choice disabled when DataManager.isAnySavefileExists() reports no save. The check runs when the choice list is built, including outside the title map. It never enables a choice already disabled by another rule and does not load a save by itself; call ET-C-LoadScreen in the selected branch.
tags.occurrences: All matching tags are removed; availability follows storage.
examples: event-title-scene tags set --target common-event:1/text:0/choice:0 --tag continue --value '"<Continue>"' --expected-hash HASH_FROM_LIST --dry-run
tags.context: Enable Coreto_4_EventTitleScene 0.1.0 with event-title-scene install after its optional providers/consumers have been arranged; the bundle must already be delivered. install selects this provider instead of VisuMZ_4_EventTitleScene and preserves other provider selections. Restart the game after configuration changes. Core Engine and Message Core are optional: if used, enable one supported provider of each before this plugin (Coreto_0_CoreEngine 0.1.0 / VisuMZ_0_CoreEngine 1.90; Coreto_1_MessageCore 0.1.0 / VisuMZ_1_MessageCore 1.57). Place it after active Options Core, Save Core, Picture Choices, VN Picture Busts, Choice Common Events and Attached Pictures, and before Message Visibility. The single-line case-insensitive tag is removed from the displayed label. Native availability checks loaded save metadata, not a successful read of the save contents; a listed file can still fail to load. A later choice list checks again. Removing the authored tag affects the next construction, not a currently displayed list. This tag belongs to Show Choices text, not Note, Comment or Show Text.
tags.writing: Use event-title-scene commands list --target common-event:1 to find Show Choices code 102 index I; message text get --target common-event:1 --index I --path choices identifies zero-based choice J. event-title-scene tags list --target common-event:1/text:I/choice:J supplies result.fileHash and occurrence indices. Replace illustrative target/index/choice 0 before writing, and use --occurrence if multiple matches exist.
